In the conversations recorded, Jake did indeed provide Li Hua with both common knowledge about the offside rule and practical techniques to avoid being in an offside position. Specifically, Jake explained the basic concept of the offside rule early in their interactions. During the initial exchange on November 5th, Jake explained that a player is offside if they are "ahead of the last defender (excluding the goalie) at the moment the ball is passed to them." He further elaborated that this rule is designed to prevent unfair advantages and maintains the flow of the game. 

Later on, in another conversation on September 3rd, Jake provided more detailed information about the offside rule, emphasizing the importance of timing and positioning. Jake highlighted that a player must not be closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-to-last opponent when the ball is played to them. He noted that understanding and applying these rules are crucial for avoiding offside penalties and maintaining fair play.

Thus, Jake did share both the common knowledge and practical techniques related to the offside rule with Li Hua, ensuring that Li Hua was fully prepared to understand and adhere to the rule in actual soccer scenarios.
